# Lab 17.2: Subscribe to a Listing

## What We Are Going to Do
Subscribe to the listing from a second project and query the linked dataset, without copying any data.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Create a second project as the "partner".**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">export PARTNER=bq-course-partner-$RANDOM
gcloud projects create $PARTNER
gcloud billing projects link $PARTNER --billing-account=$(gcloud billing projects describe $PROJECT_ID --format="value(billingAccountName)" | sed 's|billingAccounts/||')
gcloud services enable bigquery.googleapis.com analyticshub.googleapis.com --project=$PARTNER</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] Subscribe.** Switch the console to the partner project. **Sharing (Analytics Hub) → Search listings** → find **Daily Category Sales** → **Subscribe**. Name the linked dataset `partner_sales`.

3. **[SQL] Query it from the partner project.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT category, SUM(revenue) AS revenue
FROM partner_sales.daily_category_sales
GROUP BY category ORDER BY revenue DESC;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The partner pays for the query; the publisher pays for storage.

4. **[CLI] See that it is a linked dataset.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq show --format=prettyjson --project_id=$PARTNER partner_sales | grep -i -A3 linked</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[SQL] Show that it is live.** In the publisher project, insert a row:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">INSERT INTO lab17_shared.daily_category_sales VALUES (CURRENT_DATE(), 'Test', 1, 1.0);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Query again from the partner project. The new row is there at once.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Linked dataset | Read-only, zero copy |
| Freshness | Always the publisher's latest data |
| Billing | Subscriber pays for compute |
| Writes | Not allowed in the linked dataset |
